decisions.executionNote: Holder is on the right and pens on the left. Begin a gradual right-arm inward-facing side-grasp orientation, preserving the initial elbow branch.
Advance the right wrist toward the holder's outer side while finishing the inward yaw; keep fingers open and left arm stationary.
Reduce translation and yaw increments after the continuity rejection; approach the right-side holder without changing elbow branch.
Back off the wrist yaw singularity and approach the holder diagonally from its front-right side, using smaller continuous increments.
Translate toward the holder with the stable diagonal side-grasp orientation; leave the fingers open until visually aligned.
Fine-align the open right gripper around the holder's upper side using the head and wrist views.
Advance slightly along the right gripper axis and close around the holder; retention is still uncertain and will be checked visually.
The closed fingers are visibly empty. Reopen and shift laterally toward the holder on the right side of the wrist view, rather than assuming a grasp.
The holder appears to have shifted with contact rather than being centered. Withdraw the open fingers along their approach axis before another lateral alignment.
With the fingers withdrawn, shift their center toward the holder before advancing again. Keep the holder upright and avoid pushing it farther.
Turn the open gripper slightly toward the holder to center it without extending farther outward, then make a short approach.
Holder is now centered between the open fingers. Advance along the gripper axis to surround its sides before closing.
Close around the now-centered holder, then make a small lift and retreat to check that it moves with the right hand.
The holder remains centered in the wrist view during lift. Bring it back toward the shared central area while keeping the right grip closed and upright.
Continue bringing the held holder toward center-right. Begin lifting and pitching the left gripper toward a top-down pen pickup while retaining arm separation.
Park the held holder near center-right while pitching the left gripper down above the nearest white pen. Fingers remain open for visual alignment.
Align the left gripper across the nearest white pen's shaft and descend gradually. The right hand keeps the upright holder stationary.
Shift the left fingers onto the pen's shaft and lower a little further, using the wrist view to correct the lateral offset.
Fine-align along the white pen and close the left fingers on its shaft. Keep the right holder hand fixed.
Lift the grasped white pen clear of the table, then gradually turn it upright while keeping the holder stationary.
The pen stayed on the table after lifting. Reopen and return over its thicker shaft, correcting the pickup point before a lower grasp.
Lower the open left gripper around the white pen's thicker section, correcting the wrist-view rightward offset.
The descent met the table, so do not push lower. Center laterally, close on the thicker pen section, then lift straight a short distance to verify retention.
The white pen now moves with the left fingers. Lift it farther and rotate progressively toward an upright insertion orientation.
Carry the retained pen toward the holder at clearance height and finish turning its shaft vertical, with each arm staying on its own side.
Move the vertical white pen over the visible holder opening, correcting the head-view leftward offset before descending.
The pen tip is above the opening. Lower it vertically into the held upright holder, retaining the grip until it is well inside.
Seat the white pen farther inside, release it, and withdraw the left fingers upward and left while the right hand continues holding the holder.
One white pen remains in the holder after release. Move the open left hand away and reorient toward the narrow cyan marker lying closest to the holder.
Continue into a top-down approach with the left fingers aligned across the cyan marker's shaft, stopping above table height.
Descend toward the cyan marker and advance slightly along its shaft so the finger pads surround its body rather than the end.
Lower a little farther around the marker, close the left fingers, and make a small straight lift to check retention.
The marker appears pinched between the fingers. Lift and retreat from the tabletop while gradually turning it upright for insertion.
Continue lifting the retained cyan marker and rotating its shaft toward vertical, staying left of the held holder.
Finish straightening the marker and bring it over the holder opening beside the first white pen, maintaining clearance above the rim.
Lower the upright cyan marker toward the open space beside the white pen, watching for rim contact before release.
Correct the marker slightly left from the right rim, then lower it inside beside the white pen while maintaining both grips.
Seat the cyan marker a little deeper, release it inside the holder, and withdraw the open left hand while the right hand supports the holder.
Two objects remain in the held holder. Move the open left hand toward the remaining far-left cyan marker and start a top-down approach aligned with its diagonal shaft.
Finish the top-down orientation above the diagonal cyan marker and approach at clearance height with open fingers.
After the continuity stop, reduce rotation increments and lower the wrist rather than extending farther forward. Recheck alignment above the marker.
Shift the open fingers toward the marker's wrist-view leftward offset while finishing the downward pitch and lowering cautiously.
The marker is still left of the fingers and diagonal in the wrist view. Lift slightly, align the gripper across its shaft, and shift left before lowering again.
The marker is now centered. After the continuity rejection, keep orientation fixed and lower with small backward increments to reduce reach before closing.
Close on the centered cyan marker, then lift with a backward retreat to avoid the far-reach configuration. Verify that the marker follows the fingers.
The cyan marker follows the left hand. Lift and retreat toward the holder while gradually rotating its shaft upright; keep the right hand fixed.
Finish turning the retained marker vertical and carry it above the holder, keeping the left wrist on the left side and clear of the inserted pens.
Position the third pen above the open space behind the inserted cyan marker, then begin a cautious vertical descent.
Lower the third pen into the back portion of the holder, with a small inward correction from the rim and no release until seated.
Contact tilted the holder, so lift the third pen out of pressure and shift toward the empty side of the opening before retrying. Keep both grasps closed.
Clear the third pen from the rim, then gently counter-rotate the right wrist to restore the tilted holder toward upright before inserting further.
Make a smaller holder-uprighting correction and counter the third marker's visible lean. Keep the marker clear of the rim during these adjustments.
The holder is closer to upright. Correct the marker's remaining lean and move its lower end over the opening at clearance height.
The third marker is straighter and its lower end is over the empty side of the holder. Lower slowly while monitoring for renewed rim contact.
The third marker's lower end is inside the opening. Lower slightly, release it without pressing on the holder, and withdraw to check that it stays inserted.
Three pens remain in the holder after release. Move the open left hand toward the last white pen and progressively orient for a top-down grasp.
Complete the downward-facing orientation and approach the last white pen's thicker shaft with open fingers; keep the filled holder supported.
Center the last white pen between the left fingers and advance toward its thicker section while lowering carefully.
Fine-center on the last white pen's shaft, lower the finger pads to its height, close, and lift slightly while retreating from the far reach.
Lift the last white pen clear of the table and retreat while gradually rotating it upright, keeping the right hand steady.
The final white pen is retained. Finish bringing its shaft vertical and carry it toward the holder at clearance height.
Bring the final white pen over the remaining opening and lower slowly, leaving space beside the two cyan markers.
Shift the final pen toward the visible empty side of the opening rather than onto a cyan marker, then resume a short descent.
The tip contacted a cyan cap. Lift clear and reposition toward the newly visible empty rear side of the holder before another descent.
Lower the final white pen through the rear opening with no lateral pressure, retaining the grip until its tip is visibly inside.
Continue a short, slow insertion beside the existing white pen and pause to inspect whether the final tip clears the rim.
The final pen is leaning under contact rather than sliding freely. Relieve pressure and move halfway back from the rear rim to center it inside the mouth.
The final pen's lower end appears inside the mouth. Release without further pressure and withdraw to verify that all four objects remain in the holder.
The last white pen has tipped across the rim rather than settling vertically. Clear the left fingers and keep the holder still to inspect its resting position before recovery.
The final white pen fell onto the table. Reorient the open left hand for another top-down pickup of its now-horizontal shaft; keep the other three supported in the holder.
Complete the downward pickup orientation and align above the fallen white pen's cap-side shaft, stopping short of table contact.
Correct the pen's rightward wrist-view offset, lower around its shaft, and close for a second pickup.
Lift and retreat from the table to verify the new white-pen grasp, then start turning it upright without disturbing the holder.
The white pen follows the fingers. Lift it above the holder and finish turning its shaft upright for a more centered insertion.
Straighten the remaining lean and center the white pen's tip over the holder's empty area without lowering yet.
Lower the straightened white pen slowly into the visible rear opening, without lateral pressure or releasing prematurely.
